headline: Dynamical models separate measurement noise from growth and metabolic variability
label: Dynamical Modeling Under Noise
summary: Recent preprints and one published study model measurement noise explicitly alongside biological dynamics in time-series and snapshot data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is separating measurement noise and biological variability from the dynamical structure being inferred. Two items embed this directly: a biologically-informed neural network with a learnable heteroscedastic noise model, and a single-cell framework that uses the autocovariance of inferred growth rates to split measurement noise from growth-rate fluctuations. A hierarchical Bayesian ODE model applies similar logic to flow cytometry snapshots, partitioning inter- and intra-experimental heterogeneity. Other items address adjacent concerns: a model-free method drawing on over 7000 time-series features to infer parametric variation, validated on 13 simulated systems; an analysis of how isotope label number trades parameter accuracy against compute cost in lipid metabolism models; and physics-informed forecasting of COVID-19 indicators regularized by SIHR equations. What is new is joint, explicit modelling of noise structure alongside the dynamics, though the set is heterogeneous.
